subject: psychology
title: Social Influence: Foundations
welcome_lead: Why do people go along with the crowd? Begin with the basics of social influence.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology adventure on social influence foundations: conformity, obedience and types of influence.
final_note: You can name the core types of social influence and why they happen.

concepts.def: Changing behaviour to match a group.
Following a direct order from an authority.
Conforming to be liked or fit in.
Conforming because others seem to know more.
Public and private acceptance of group view.

walkthroughs.body_html: Conformity is changing to match a peer group (no order needed). Obedience is following a direct order from a higher-status authority. Conformity is usually horizontal; obedience is vertical.

walkthroughs.h2: Why we conform: NSI and ISI
walkthroughs.body_html: Deutsch & Gerard's two-process theory: NSI (normative) — we conform to be liked and avoid rejection. ISI (informational) — we conform because we think the group is right, especially in ambiguous situations.

Compliance: go along publicly, disagree privately. Identification: change views while in the group. Internalisation: genuine, lasting change in private belief. Each level reflects how deep the influence runs.
